spiritual_reading:
# Spiritual Translation: The Eighteen Governing Principles of the Lord's Order

---

**¶1:** Eighteen [GAP-1: governing principles of authority over all successive states of the Lord's kingdom] exist and are appointed, established in eighteen distinct degrees of spiritual life. Nine among them [GAP-2: are ordained within] the interior heavenly states, while nine exist throughout the states where spiritual life has suffered injury and corruption.

---

**¶2:** The first governing principle is the sovereignty of the Divine Itself, the God of divine truth, the supreme dominion over all interior states of celestial life — the One who Is; who is established [GAP-3: in absolute self-subsistence], He alone, in His own essence, [GAP-4: dwelling in unapproachable infinity] apart from all that proceeds from Him. This is the first governing principle [GAP-5: of all spiritual order], the one that surpasses every other sovereignty.

---

**¶3:** The second governing principle is that of the Divine Love that gives life — the glorified origin of all influx that has ever proceeded into the states of this world's spiritual existence.

---

**¶4:** The third governing principle is established for the most interior celestial state — the primordial human will united to the Divine. This is the state that humbled and overcame the entire original opposition of falsity from evil, which had dominion in the realms of spiritual darkness.

---

**¶5:** The fourth governing principle belongs to the Divine Love cherished within all illumination — the great and honored affection of good within the interior states of celestial life.

---

**¶6:** The fifth governing principle is that of the Divine Ordering Intelligence — the great architect of providence who constructed a new state of spiritual life as a renewal, as [GAP-6: a dwelling place of good] for [GAP-7: all] the originating states of wisdom; and also as a means of restraint and confinement for the power of evil and all its derivative falsities.

---

**¶7:** The sixth governing principle is that of the Divine Operative Power — the [GAP-8: glorified] mighty agency that raised up the most interior celestial state out of the [GAP-9: depths of falsity and evil]; who also set in order and constructed the external states of spiritual life [GAP-10: as an arrangement] both for a purification of wisdom from its contaminations, [GAP-11: and] for a binding [GAP-12: of the] powers of opposition and hostility.

---

**¶8:** The seventh governing principle is that of the Divine Mediating Principle — the sovereign of the intermediate sphere, and the master of all counsels of wisdom by which the interiors communicate with the exteriors.

---

**¶9:** The eighth governing principle is that of Divine Truth in its radiance, who [GAP-13: is] the liberator and redeemer [GAP-14: of] all the interiors of the human mind.

---

**¶10:** The ninth governing principle is that of the Divine Understanding — the universal intelligence to whom all forms of the church shall be gathered; and all the [GAP-15: spiritual life] that will be purified from the natural state returns to this intelligence as to its source.

---

**¶11:** These are the nine governing principles of the celestial order, ordained in the interior heavenly states and established for the originating degrees of the Lord's glorified kingdom — [GAP-16: within the dominion of the sovereignty of] divine honor.

---

**¶12:** In contrast, these are the other nine governing principles that are ordained and operative within this intermediate sphere of spiritual conflict.

---

**¶13:** Three governing principles reside within the doctrine of enlightenment: one belongs to the Divine Mediating Principle, the second to the Divine Operative Power, the third to the Divine Power that rescues and orders.

---

**¶14:** Again, there are another three within the doctrine that [GAP-17: operates in states of spiritual obscurity]: the first is the sovereignty of Divine Truth in its radiance, [GAP-18: the second is that of] the most interior celestial will, the third is that of the pure affection of truth in its innocence. These six governing principles are established within the two doctrinal vessels — the one that carries the mind through illuminated states and the one that carries the mind through states of darkness.

---

**¶15:** The seventh governing principle is established in the highest degree of the rational mind — the interior firmament that separates heavenly perception from natural thought. The great sovereignty of divine honor presides upon it.

---

**¶16:** The eighth governing principle is established in the external natural mind. The Divine Truth that judges sits upon it — the truth that discriminates in all human willing and thinking. Three ways of life are distinguished before this judgment: one leading to spiritual death, one leading to spiritual life, and one leading to the mixed state where good and evil remain intermingled and undetermined.

---

**¶17:** The ninth governing principle, ordained and established in this sphere, belongs to the one sent forth — the apostolic function of divine teaching that enters directly into natural life.

---

**¶18:** These are the nine great governing [GAP-19: principles of spiritual authority] that are established in this sphere of [GAP-20: spiritual conflict and restoration, mirroring the interior order] of the Lord's glorified kingdom, the one that the [GAP-21: successive states of regeneration] honor [GAP-22: through reception of influx from the interior degrees] and the [GAP-23: conjunction of good and truth in the external life of the church].

reconstructions.reconstructed_text: Eighteen [great thrones for all the fathers] exist and are appointed, which are established in eighteen places! While there are nine among them [appointed in] the outer aeons, they exist [i]n all the worlds of the damage.

The first throne is the throne of the Father, the God of [trut]h, the King of the aeons of greatness, the one who exists; who is established [in himself] he alone, in his own essen[c]e, [dwelling] apart. This is the first throne [of all] the one that surpasses all the thrones.
The second throne is that of the [gl]orious Mother of Life. She is the origin of all the emanations that have come to this world.
The third throne is constructed for the father, the First Man. He is the one who humiliated the entire first enmity, which existed in the worlds of Darkness.
The fourth throne is that of the Beloved of the Lights, the great honoured Beloved of the aeons of greatness.

The fifth throne is that of the glorious Great Builder; the great architect who built the new aeon for a newness, for [a resting place] for [the] fathers of light; also for a place of binding and a prison for the enemy and his powers.

[The sixth thro]n[e] is that of the Living Spirit, the [glorious] mighty one, he who bore up the First Man out from the [land of Darkness]; who also set in order and constructed the world [s ...] both for a cleansing of the light, [and] for a binding [of the] powers of the enmity.
The seventh th[rone is] that of the Third Ambassador, the king of the zone, also the master of all advices.
The eighth throne is that of Jesus the Splendour, who [is] the releaser and redeemer [of] all souls.
The ninth throne is the throne of the great M[ind, he to whom] all the churches shall gather; and all the [life] that will be purified from the world returns to him.
These are the nine thrones of ho[no]u[r] appointed in the outer aeo[ns], <which are established> for the fathers of the glorious realm; [in the kingdom of the King of] Honour.
In contrast, these are the other nine thrones that are appointed in this world of the zone.
Three thrones in the ship of [the d]ay: one is that of the Ambassador, the second i[s that of] the Great Spirit, the third is that of the Living Spirit.

Once again, there are another three in the ship that [belongs to the night]: the first is the throne of Jesus the Splendour, [the second is that of] the First Man, the third is tha[t of the Virgin of] Light. These six thrones are established in the two ships.
Also, the seventh throne is established in the seventh firmament. The great King of Honour sits upon it.

The eighth throne is established in the atmosphere. The Judge of truth sits upon it, he who judges all mankind. Three paths shall be distinguished before him: one to death, one to life, on[e] to the mingling.
The ninth throne appointed and established is for the [a]postle.
Th[ese] are the [nin]e great [th]ro[nes of honour] that are established in this world of [the zone] of the glorious realm, the one that the [... ...] honour them [... ...] and the [...].

fills.original: great thrones for all the fathers
fills.explanation: The chapter enumerates eighteen thrones belonging to the divine fathers of the Manichaean cosmology; "great thrones for all the fathers" is the standard Kephalaia phrasing for these governing seats of authority.
The verb "appointed" is used throughout this chapter for the establishment of thrones, and "appointed in" introduces the location (the outer aeons) where these nine thrones are ordained.

The spiritual reading indicates "absolute self-subsistence"; in the Kephalaia register, the Father's throne is established "in himself" — grounded in his own being — reinforced by the following phrase "he alone, in his own essence."
The spiritual reading describes the Father as "dwelling in unapproachable infinity apart"; "dwelling apart" captures the Father's active self-existence in separation from all that proceeds from him.
The spiritual reading says "of all spiritual order"; in the Kephalaia register "of all" universalizes the first throne's supremacy, fitting the clause "the one that surpasses all the thrones."

The spiritual reading indicates "a dwelling place of good"; in Manichaean cosmology, the new aeon built by the Great Builder serves as a "resting place" (ma mton) for the redeemed light entities — the fathers of light.
The article "the" is grammatically required before "fathers of light," which is a standard fixed epithet in the Kephalaia requiring its article.
The Living Spirit is regularly given the epithet "glorious" in the Kephalaia; the spiritual reading confirms "glorified mighty agency," and "glorious" is the standard natural-plane equivalent.

"Land of Darkness" is the standard Manichaean term for the realm from which the Living Spirit rescued the First Man; the spiritual reading's "depths of falsity and evil" corresponds precisely to this natural-plane designation.
The conjunction "and" is required to connect the two parallel purpose clauses: "for a cleansing of the light, and for a binding of the powers."
The genitive construction "of the" links "binding" to "powers of the enmity," which is the standard Kephalaia phrase for the subjugation of the dark archons.
The copula "is" introduces the predicate identifying Jesus the Splendour as "the releaser and redeemer," matching the standard Kephalaia identification formula.
The preposition "of" connects "redeemer" to "all souls," forming the standard Kephalaia soteriological formula describing Jesus the Splendour's function.
In the Kephalaia, the Great Mind receives all purified "life" (light-life) returning from the world; "life" is the standard natural-plane term for what the spiritual reading calls "spiritual life."

fills.original: in the kingdom of the King of
fills.explanation: The King of Honour is a standard Manichaean divine figure; "in the kingdom of the King of Honour" correctly locates the nine heavenly thrones within his dominion, matching the spiritual reading's "within the dominion of the sovereignty of divine honor."
The two cosmic ships in Manichaean cosmology are the ship of the day (sun) and the ship of the night (moon); "belongs to the night" correctly identifies the second vessel.
This follows the enumeration formula used throughout the chapter ("the first is..., the second is that of..., the third is...") and is structurally required to introduce the First Man's throne.

Completing "thro-" + "nes of honour" = "thrones of honour," directly paralleling ¶11's "thrones of honour appointed in the outer aeons" — the same epithet applied to the corresponding set of worldly thrones.

"This world of the zone" is the standard Kephalaia designation for the cosmic sphere of mixture where light and darkness contend; it appears in ¶12 ("this world of the zone") and is the natural-plane equivalent of the spiritual reading's "sphere of spiritual conflict."
